cf.title: Stack-based tracking of per-node WAL/buffer usage

input.subject: Stack-based tracking of per-node WAL/buffer usage

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at level 1a or 1b: the problem is stated, measured, and wanted by several reviewers. The surviving objections are fixable design points at level 2. replication-ondisk-1 asks for a backstop when an extension calls InstrStart without abort handling, and maintenance-fit-1 asks for a committed test that catches lost abort-time totals. The abort model needs sign-off from a committer who knows the executor and resource owners.

brief.title: Stack-based tracking of per-node WAL and buffer usage
brief.problem: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) is slow because InstrStopNode diffs the global pgBufferUsage/pgWalUsage counters with BufferUsageAccumDiff for every node cycle. The author also wants a base for later work, such as estimated distinct buffer hits and separate index and table buffer counts in index scans.
brief.proposed_design: Buffer and WAL counter updates write into the current entry of a per-backend instrumentation stack; each node pushes a zeroed entry on start, pops it on stop, and adds it to its parent at finalize. Aborts are handled by QueryInstrumentation through resource owners and a dedicated memory context, or by PG_TRY/PG_FINALLY. Later patches retire pgBufferUsage, specialize ExecProcNodeInstr per option set, and show table buffers for index scans.
user_visible_surface: EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows a new "Table Buffers" line for Index Scan and Index Only Scan, counted in "Buffers" as well.
Structured EXPLAIN output gets "Table Buffers" and "Table I/O Timings" groups.
C API: global pgBufferUsage and BufferUsageAccumDiff are removed; extensions must use InstrStart/InstrStop instead.
C API: QueryDesc totaltime is renamed and now allocated by ExecutorStart, with an options field set by extensions (already pushed).
C API: new QueryInstrumentation, NodeInstrumentation, TriggerInstrumentation structs and INSTR_BUFUSAGE_*/INSTR_WALUSAGE_* macros.
author_claims: The stack cuts EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS ON, TIMING OFF) overhead on a large COUNT(*) from about 35% to about 20% of runtime.
Specialized ExecProcNodeInstr roughly halves TIMING OFF, BUFFERS OFF overhead, from about 13% to about 6%.
Top-level totals stay correct after aborts, including caught errors in functions and triggers.
Separate table buffer counts help find whether index or table access makes a query slow, a benefit Andres Freund also named.
brief.thread_state: Andres Freund pushed several preparatory patches for 19 and deferred the stack patch to 20, asking for senior architectural review; Heikki Linnakangas still finds the stack and tree model confusing. v18 (October 2026) reworks the series and has no visible reply yet.
unclear: The material does not show overhead numbers for WAL ON, or for workloads other than a large COUNT(*).
Naming of "Table Buffers" versus the existing "Heap Fetches" and "Heap Blocks" is still open.
The patch keeps pgWalUsage, and the material does not say when or how that global will be retired.
The material does not say whether the test_session_buffer_usage module is meant for commit.
The material does not say how the patch affects extensions that read pgBufferUsage directly.

prior_attempts.title: Reduce timing overhead of EXPLAIN ANALYZE using rdtsc
prior_attempts.quote: Since the author or no one else showed interest in taking it forward and the patch had no activity for more than 1 year, I have changed the status to RWF.
prior_attempts.reason: The thread stopped after the v8 patch of February 2023, and nobody continued the work for about a year. vignesh C closed the entry as Returned with feedback because neither the author nor anyone else took it forward. Earlier, Andres Freund doubted the patch was ready on reliability and code complexity, citing the Linux-only restriction, but the entry closed from inactivity.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P1 cut the timing cost of EXPLAIN ANALYZE by reading the TSC. This proposal cuts the buffer and WAL counting cost by replacing the BufferUsageAccumDiff diff with a stack. P1 closed from inactivity, and this thread is active at v18.

prior_attempts.title: Sampling-based timing for EXPLAIN ANALYZE
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P22 tried to lower EXPLAIN ANALYZE overhead by sampling timings. This proposal keeps exact per-node counts and changes how buffer and WAL usage reach each node. No reason is recorded for P22.

objections.title: Extension callers of the plain Instrumentation API can leave a dangling stack
objections.failure_scenario: An extension that read pgBufferUsage switches to InstrStart/InstrStop as the 0005 commit message advises, but adds no PG_TRY/PG_FINALLY. An error between the two calls leaves instr_stack.current pointing at memory freed by the abort. Later buffer and WAL counter updates in the same backend write into that freed memory, and nothing reports it.
objections.argument: The 0005 commit message says plain Instrumentation "requires appropriate abort handling in all cases", and the 0004 message limits abort safety to QueryInstrumentation or explicit PG_TRY/PG_FINALLY. Message #26 confirms that without this reset the stack is corrupted after an abort. The material shows no backstop, such as a reset to instr_top or an assertion in AbortTransaction, for callers that get this wrong. Today an extension that diffs pgBufferUsage cannot corrupt memory this way, so the API change turns a counting mistake into a safety bug.
objections.author_must_show: What resets or checks instr_stack at transaction abort or error recovery when an extension calls InstrStart without PG_FINALLY or a resource owner?

critic.reasoning: The 0005 commit message sends extensions to InstrStart/InstrStop and leaves abort handling to the caller. The visible material shows no reset of the stack at transaction abort for a caller that uses neither a resource owner nor PG_FINALLY.

objections.title: Lost abort-time totals are caught only by a test module not meant for commit
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a new kind of instrumentation, for example per-trigger or per-receiver, and does not register it as a child of the QueryInstrumentation. When that code errors out, its buffer activity is not added to the parent. Regression tests pass, and session or pg_stat_statements totals undercount without any visible error.
objections.argument: The trigger case in messages #21 and #23 and the EXPLAIN (SERIALIZE) case in message #15 were both missing from abort accounting. Both were found only through test_session_buffer_usage, which the author calls test-only and not meant for commit (messages #11, #19, #32). Message #26 says a stack that is not reset does fail regression tests, but lost accumulation does not. Once pgBufferUsage is retired in 0005, these abort totals are the only session-level number, so a silent loss is harder to spot than it is today.
objections.author_must_show: Which committed test fails when a new instrumentation user skips registering with its QueryInstrumentation and then errors out?

critic.reasoning: The 0003 tests cover abort cases visible in EXPLAIN, but the lost trigger totals in message #23 showed up only through the test module. Messages #11 and #32 leave open whether that module is committed.

objections.title: Two counting models remain, buffers on the stack and WAL on a global
objections.failure_scenario: A developer adds a new counter, or moves pgstat WAL accounting, and has to decide between the stack and pgWalUsage. INSTR_WALUSAGE_ADD writes both. If a fix updates only one of the two paths, pg_stat_wal and EXPLAIN WAL numbers drift apart, and nobody notices until a user compares them.
objections.argument: The 0005 commit message keeps pgWalUsage because pgstat and heap_page_prune_and_freeze depend on it, and message #3 calls removing it "interesting". The material gives no plan or release for retiring it. Every WAL record now updates two places, and the thread shows no measurements with WAL ON. Message #49 also cites an existing pg_stat_wal bug around these globals.
objections.author_must_show: What is the plan and target release for retiring pgWalUsage, and what does WAL ON overhead measure today?

critic.reasoning: The drift scenario is weak because INSTR_WALUSAGE_ADD updates both places in one macro. But the material gives no plan for retiring pgWalUsage and no WAL ON numbers for the stack patch, so those two requests stand.

objections.title: "Table Buffers" label adds a third name next to "Heap" fields
objections.failure_scenario: Release 20 ships "Table Buffers" next to "Heap Fetches" and "Heap Blocks". Plan visualizers and log parsers then match on the text label and the JSON group key. A later rename to fix the inconsistency breaks those tools, so the project keeps the mixed naming for good.
objections.argument: In message #11 the author asks whether "Table Buffers" fits with "Heap Fetches" and "Heap Blocks", and message #12 says this is still open. v18 keeps the label, and structured output gets the new "Table Buffers" and "Table I/O Timings" groups (message #17). EXPLAIN labels and JSON keys are a contract that external tools read, so the naming should be settled before commit.
objections.author_must_show: Which naming will EXPLAIN use for table access across nodes, and will "Heap Fetches" and "Heap Blocks" be renamed or kept?

critic.reasoning: Message #12 says the naming question is still open, and v18 ships "Table Buffers" next to "Heap Fetches" and "Heap Blocks". Andres Freund's "s/heap/table/" in message #7 is about a code comment and does not settle the EXPLAIN label.

refuted.title: Removing pgBufferUsage breaks extensions and splits buffer and WAL APIs
refuted.failure_scenario: An extension that snapshots pgBufferUsage in its executor hooks and diffs it with BufferUsageAccumDiff stops compiling on Postgres 20. A port to InstrStart/InstrStop that leaves out PG_TRY/PG_FINALLY leaves the instrumentation stack inconsistent after an error. The author finds out from wrong totals or a crash in a later query.
refuted.argument: The 0005 commit message removes pgBufferUsage and BufferUsageAccumDiff and sends extensions to InstrStart/InstrStop, with abort handling as the caller's job. pgWalUsage stays as a global for pgstat and pruning, so out-of-tree code ends up with one counter set read by diffing and its sibling read through the stack. Message #46 accepts one more round of extension churn for the totaltime rename, but the material does not say whether pgWalUsage moves later or when. Without that, extension authors may have to port twice.
refuted.author_must_show: Which out-of-tree users read pgBufferUsage today, and will pgWalUsage move to the stack in the same release so extension authors port only once?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1 (port without PG_FINALLY) and maintenance-fit-2 (pgWalUsage stays a global). The remaining point, a compile break in a major release, is loud and is normal practice for extension APIs.

refuted.title: Removing pgBufferUsage moves abort-safety work onto every extension
refuted.failure_scenario: An extension that snapshots pgBufferUsage around a hook stops compiling on upgrade. Its author switches to InstrStart/InstrStop but does not add PG_TRY/PG_FINALLY. The first caught error inside that section leaves the instrumentation stack inconsistent for the rest of the backend.
refuted.argument: Under 0005, every Instrumentation user must handle aborts through the resource owner or PG_FINALLY, and pgBufferUsage and BufferUsageAccumDiff are removed. The pgBufferUsage removal and the 0004 performance gain are separate commits, so the retirement step is not required for the speedup. The brief notes that the material does not say how extensions that read pgBufferUsage directly are affected.
refuted.author_must_show: Could the cheap global session counter stay for read-only consumers, and which known extensions would break under 0005?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1, which states the same failure scenario with more detail on the missing reset.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: 0002 changes how xlog.c updates WAL usage counters, and 0004 touches replication/logical/worker.c; no WAL record changes.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: 0005 removes pgBufferUsage and BufferUsageAccumDiff and adds QueryInstrumentation, NodeInstrumentation and the INSTR_* macros.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: see objection standards-compat-2: "Table Buffers" label adds a third name next to "Heap" fields

touch_points.label: psql UX conventions
touch_points.reason: 0007 adds a "Table Buffers" line and structured "Table Buffers" and "Table I/O Timings" groups to EXPLAIN ANALYZE output.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The series rewrites instrument.c and the counter updates in bufmgr.c, so later back-patched fixes in those areas will not apply cleanly.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Every new instrumentation user must handle aborts through a resource owner or PG_TRY/PG_FINALLY, and pgWalUsage stays as a second counting model.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: Buffer and WAL counter updates in bufmgr.c, localbuf.c and xlog.c now write through the current instrumentation stack entry.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: What resets or checks instr_stack at transaction abort when an extension calls InstrStart without PG_TRY/PG_FINALLY or a resource owner?
Which committed test fails when a new instrumentation user does not register with its QueryInstrumentation and then errors out?
Is test_session_buffer_usage meant for commit, and if not, what replaces its coverage of top-level totals after aborts?
What is the plan and target release for retiring pgWalUsage, and what overhead does the stack patch show with WAL ON?
Which naming will EXPLAIN use for table access across nodes, and will "Heap Fetches" and "Heap Blocks" be renamed or kept?

committability.owner_note: Andres Freund pushed the preparatory patches and reviewed the stack design, and Heikki Linnakangas reviewed an earlier version. The stack patch still needs a committer who knows executor instrumentation, resource owners and abort handling; v18 has no reply yet.
committability.liability: The owner signs for correct buffer and WAL totals after every abort path, in EXPLAIN, pg_stat_statements, VACUUM and parallel workers, and for the extension API break. That liability lasts as long as the stack model exists, and it grows with each new instrumentation user.
committability.author_follow_up: Strong sign that the author stays: 18 versions over 14 months, feedback addressed in each round, and the entry moved forward by the author in October 2026.

priority.reason: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) users and tools like pg_stat_statements gain from the lower overhead, and two reviewers want the table buffer split. The series is eight patches across the executor, buffer manager, WAL insertion and several access methods, and the abort model adds rules that future instrumentation users must follow.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the abort handling, the resource owner release order and the parallel worker accumulation could not be checked. The README hunk was truncated, and only 3 of 49 messages were shown, so later answers in the thread may already cover some questions.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Reduce timing overhead of EXPLAIN ANALYZE using rdtsc
precedents_retrieved.authors: Andres Freund (andresfreund), Lukas Fittl (lfittl), David Geier (geidav)
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make instr_time count CPU reference cycles read with rdtsc, which does not wait for prior instructions, and convert cycles to time only on output, to cut the timing overhead of EXPLAIN ANALYZE. The patch uses rdtsc only on Linux/x86 when the kernel clocksource is tsc, takes the TSC frequency from CPUID, and falls back to clock_gettime() otherwise.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The thread stopped after the v8 patch of February 2023, and nobody continued the work for about a year. vignesh C closed the entry as Returned with feedback because neither the author nor anyone else took it forward. Earlier, Andres Freund doubted the patch was ready on reliability and code complexity, citing the Linux-only restriction, but the entry closed from inactivity.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Since the author or no one else showed interest in taking it forward
and the patch had no activity for more than 1 year, I have changed the
status to RWF.

precedents_retrieved.title: minimizing pg_stat_statements.track='none' performance overhead
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pgss_post_parse_analyze in pg_stat_statements return early when pgss_enabled() is false, so that pg_stat_statements.track = 'none' skips query jumbling and query text storage. The goal is to cut the extension's overhead without a restart to remove it from shared_preload_libraries.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last message reports that the same patch has two commitfest entries (2080 and 2092) and asks which one to keep, so this entry may have been withdrawn as a duplicate. Robert Haas asked what happens if pgss_enabled() changes between processing stages, but no message treats this as blocking.

precedents_retrieved.title: Support SK_SEARCHNULL / SK_SEARCHNOTNULL for heap-only scans
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes heap scans honor SK_SEARCHNULL and SK_SEARCHNOTNULL scan keys in HeapKeyTest(), which skey.h documents as supported only for index scans. The goal was convenience for extensions that scan tables directly without SPI; a later follow-up by Jacob Champion added planner pushdown of IS [NOT] NULL quals into Seq Scan as scan keys.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas saw no benefit in heapam support alone and asked that nodeSeqScan.c use it, with performance results, and that the table AM API get an 'amsearchnulls' field. The author wanted to defer the executor part to a later patch, so Heikki marked the entry Returned with Feedback. The later executor and planner patches got no visible review before the entry closed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Ok, I don't think this patch on its own is a good idea, without the
other parts, so I'll mark this as Returned with Feedback in the commitfest.

precedents_retrieved.title: explain_regress, explain(MACHINE), and default to explain(BUFFERS)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch series adds a GUC explain_regress, set on by pg_regress, that turns off TIMING, SUMMARY, COSTS and BUFFERS, so that BUFFERS can become the default for EXPLAIN without changing regression output. An optional explain(MACHINE) option hides machine-dependent EXPLAIN ANALYZE output such as memory use, sort details and Heap Fetches.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that making EXPLAIN behave differently for developers and tests than for users may cause confusion and hide bugs. He also noted that the GUC had no documentation, that MACHINE is an unclear option name, that the GUC is not applied under make installcheck, and that the postgres_fdw change can break older postgres_fdw versions talking to new servers. The author then suggested closing the entry until someone finds another way to enable BUFFERS by default.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Making
EXPLAIN work significantly differently for developers and test
critters than it does for everyone else seems likely to promote
confusion and hide bugs.

precedents_retrieved.title: Subtrans performance smoothing
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch reduces pg_subtrans lookups after a snapshot overflows its subxid cache, so a few overflowed backends do not slow down XidInMVCCSnapshot() for every session. It checks the snapshot before subtrans, keeps full subxid data in snapshots, uses binary search on standby snapshots, and makes GetTopmostTransaction check xmin as it walks.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch from the commitfest in favour of his other patch, "Minimizing calls to SubTransSetParent()". Andres Freund had argued that subtrans needs a redesign, such as an in-memory hashtable in place of the SLRU, and that patches that only improve things at the margins are not a good use of time. Robert Haas and the author disputed that redesign, and the withdrawal message does not cite the objection as the reason.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
To avoid confusion, I will withdraw this patch from the CF, in favour
of my other patch on a similar topic,
Minimizing calls to SubTransSetParent()
https://commitfest.postgresql.org/39/3806/.

precedents_retrieved.title: Flush SLRU counters in checkpointer process
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes the checkpointer report SLRU statistics during normal operation instead of only at server shutdown. After review it moved the WAL and SLRU stats reports into pgstat_report_checkpointer(), so they also run from CheckpointWriteDelay().
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch's new pg_stat_slru test failed on Windows CI in 031_recovery_conflict. The author traced this to a race on have_slrustats and said a more stable version would follow, but none was posted. The entry was then returned with feedback, which message #9 gives as a consensus to prioritise other patches because this one was not in good shape.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
There
are many patches to be reviewed and this one doesn't seem to be in the
best shape, so we have to prioritise.

precedents_retrieved.title: Track Oldest Initialized WAL Buffer Page
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an OldestInitializedPage field to XLogCtl that tracks the start address of the oldest initialized WAL buffer page, updated under WALBufMappingLock. Its purpose is to let callers check quickly, without a lock, whether a WAL record is still in the WAL buffers, and to walk the buffers from oldest to newest.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas showed that a caller can already check whether a record is in WAL buffers by comparing xlblocks[idx] with the expected page end pointer, with an atomic read if stale results are fine. He saw no need to track OldestInitializedPage. The author did not reply, and the entry was returned with feedback after the thread stalled.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
But I don't see the point of tracking OldestInitializedPage. It
seems cheap enough that we could, if there's a need for it, but I don't
see the need.

precedents_retrieved.title: KnownAssignedXidsGetAndSetXmin performance
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch reduces the cost of scanning the KnownAssignedXids array when a hot standby builds snapshots while a long transaction runs on the primary. Early versions added a next-valid-entry offset array; the final version, from Simon Riggs, compresses the array more often, once every 64 removed xids.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The thread does not state the reason for the decision. On the day of the decision, Tom Lane wrote that he could not reproduce the original complaint on v13 or HEAD. He saw KnownAssignedXidsGetAndSetXmin under 1% of CPU, and not growing. He also asked whether the spinlock could be replaced with memory barriers, and the entry was returned with feedback that day.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I do see KnownAssignedXidsGetAndSetXmin eating a bit of time in the standby backends, but it's under 1% and doesn't seem to be rising over time.

precedents_retrieved.title: In bitmap scan explain node show how many relevant heap pages were not examined
precedents_retrieved.summary:
In bitmap scan explain node show how many relevant heap pages were not examined
Threads: improve transparency of bitmap-only heap scans

roaster_notes.note: No listed precedent was rejected for a reason that applies here. P1 closed from inactivity, while this author has posted 18 versions and had parts committed. P22 and P24 have no recorded reason. Message #13 points to an earlier thread only as the source of the count(*) benchmark.
There is no SQL-level syntax, GUC or pg_dump change. The EXPLAIN option set is unchanged, and "Buffers" still includes table access, so existing totals stay comparable.

The proposal changes no on-disk format, WAL record, wire protocol message or catalog, so pg_upgrade, standbys and subscribers are not affected. The pointer in shared parallel instrumentation (message #43) was answered in message #44. The nbtree VACUUM invariant does not apply, because nbtsort.c is only touched for instrumentation.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. It changes how per-backend buffer and WAL counters are collected, and EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows them only to a user who could already run the query and see its total Buffers. The new instrumentation memory and stack are per backend, freed at query end or abort, and limited by the nesting depth that the executor already enforces.

The nbtree VACUUM invariant does not apply, because nbtsort.c is touched only for parallel build instrumentation. The stop on understandability (message #37, Heikki) and the open request for senior review (message #34) belong to other angles.

Postgres has no existing way to get per-node buffer or WAL counts without the BufferUsageAccumDiff cost, and an extension cannot replace how the buffer manager counts. pg_statio_user_tables splits heap and index blocks only per table and cumulatively, so it cannot replace per-node Table Buffers under concurrency.

The material shows real demand. EXPLAIN ANALYZE overhead is a long-standing pain that a committer has pursued since 2020 ([P1]), and Andres Freund calls the design a large improvement (message #34). Tomas Vondra and Andres both want separate table buffer counts for index scans (messages #2, #18). Costs on non-users, extension API churn and the abort model belong to other angles.
